correctness.rationale: The variable-step BDF2 zero-test equation gives precisely q(R)=R²/(1+2R). Stationary two-state ergodic products decay a.s. because ab<1. Positive series L^s convergence is equivalent to rho(diag(a^s,b^s) P)<1: exponential moment bounds prove sufficiency, and conditional perpetuity plus strict Perron left eigenvector proves necessity, including equality and p=0. The determinant is affine in p, crosses zero once for r>1+sqrt(2), and stays positive in the stable branch; exact fractions 24/31 and 171/283 checked by standalone script. Numerical tests are corroboration only. Limits: zero test equation, exact arithmetic, infinite horizon.

value.rationale: The parameter r is a natural ratio contrast and p measures run persistence at unchanged stationary ratio frequencies. The exact all-real-s moment boundary distinguishes pathwise zero-test stability from moment blow-up; e.g. r=3,p=0.7 gives finite expected amplification but infinite variance. This can guide correlated random time-step diagnostics and identifies a structural reliability question absent from finite-grid stability claims; no broad ODE error theorem is asserted.
